title: Copilot Cowork: access Business Applications through Work IQ and use business skills
summary: Hold: the spending-control API only lists policies and cannot set a spending limit. The skill-control automation deletes a skill permanently rather than deactivating it; Microsoft documents a non-destructive state update. The roadmap dates, preview qualification, admin-installed default and consumption billing are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans access to Business Applications through Work IQ in Cowork and Business Skills for end-to-end business processes.
claims.quote: Users can access Business Applications through Work IQ in Copilot Cowork and use Business Skills to complete end-to-end business processes grounded in their enterprise data and apps.

claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)", "Microsoft Dataverse", "Work IQ"]

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: The plugin is admin-opt-in: users cannot add it until an administrator installs it for them.
claims.quote: An admin must install the Business apps (preview) plugin for users. Users can't add the plugin in Cowork until an admin installs it for them.

claims.claim: Power Apps model-driven apps are available as Business Applications in Work IQ.
claims.quote: Power Apps model-driven apps are available as Business Applications in Work IQ.

claims.claim: Work IQ uses an app's views, forms and tables to complete requests.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses the app's views, forms, and tables to complete the request.

claims.claim: Business skills are business-process instructions saved in a Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: The business skill is saved in the environment you used to connect to the Dataverse MCP server or a relevant environment through Work IQ.

claims.claim: After creation and activation, Copilot Chat, Cowork and connected agents can discover and use skills the user can access.
claims.quote: After you create and activate business skills in your environment, Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork, and connected agents can discover and use the skills you have access to and follow your organization's processes.

claims.claim: Learn documents Cowork access as public preview, despite the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: Access through Cowork is available in public preview.

claims.claim: Access to Business Applications through Work IQ MCP is generally available.
claims.quote: Access to Business Applications through Work IQ Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Microsoft Copilot Studio is generally available.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments, subject to exceptions.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions:
claims.fix: Add: 'The general feature-settings reference still lists the Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) settings as Off by default: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/settings-features#dataverse-intelligence-preview.' Retain the newer, specific default-settings guidance.

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: The plan to enable existing environments was deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptionshas been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The tenant audience offers All users, Specific groups and No users, with All users the default.
claims.quote: To turn off access for everyone, select No users. To turn on access for everyone, select All users. This option is the default. To provide access to a limited audience, select Specific groups

claims.where: controls[2].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ participation settings do not prevent agentic access to environment data.
claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data. Use App Access controls to manage that access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ respects existing Dataverse permissions and does not grant additional business-data access.
claims.quote: If the app appears but data is missing, confirm your Dataverse security roles and record access. Work IQ doesn't grant additional access to business data.

claims.claim: For US tenants using FedRAMP-accredited environments, enabling Work IQ might send data outside the FedRAMP authorization boundary.
claims.quote: Enabling Work IQ might cause data to flow from the tenant's FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365, which is outside the applicable FedRAMP authorization boundary.

claims.claim: Connecting the plugin involves selecting credentials and entering the sign-in number in Authenticator.
claims.quote: Select your credentials. A number appears to approve your sign in request. Enter the number in the Authenticator app.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; controls[3]
claims.claim: App Access controls which applications, including Cowork, can access an environment's data.
claims.quote: App Access is the mechanism used to choose which applications, including agentic applications such as Copilot Cowork, are allowed to access data in a particular environment.

claims.claim: Business skills are user-owned by default.
claims.quote: Skills are user-owned by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Skills can be shared with everyone in the environment.
claims.quote: General access—Makes the skill available to everyone in the environment.

claims.claim: Access through a shared security role requires both that security role and Skill Sharing Role.
claims.quote: An administrator must assign users the Skill Sharing Role, either directly or through a team. Users must also have the security role that the skill is shared with.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ can create and update business records.
claims.quote: For example, ask Work IQ to list records from an app view, show the details of a record, create a record with the values in your prompt, or update an existing record.

claims.claim: Users review proposed changes and explicitly confirm before the operation is submitted.
claims.quote: For an operation that changes data, review the proposed values, make any needed changes, and explicitly confirm the operation before it's submitted.

claims.claim: Delete operations also require explicit confirmation.
claims.quote: Delete operations also require explicit confirmation.

claims.claim: Skills can be created or updated through Copilot or a connected agent.
claims.quote: You can also create and update skills through Copilot or an agent connected to Work IQ or the Dataverse MCP server

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends testing skills with repeatable scenarios before sharing them broadly.
claims.quote: Test each skill with a repeatable scenario before you share it broadly.

claims.claim: Create and update operations are unavailable when the selected form has JavaScript OnLoad, OnChange or OnSave handlers.
claims.quote: You can't create or update a record when the selected form has JavaScript OnLoad, OnChange, or OnSave event handlers.

claims.claim: Custom controls are not supported.
claims.quote: Custom controls and subgrids aren't supported.

claims.claim: Subgrids are not supported.
claims.quote: Custom controls and subgrids aren't supported.

claims.claim: The Business skills page does not currently display per-skill runtime usage or feedback.
claims.quote: The Business skills page doesn't currently show per-skill runtime usage or feedback. Use controlled test cases and any logs or traces provided by the agent experience to collect evidence.

claims.where: licensing.notes; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Business-context consumption supporting a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork: Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.where: front matter: cost; licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature's consumption is metered in Copilot Credits, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing (UBB) charges for consumption rather than simply enabling a feature. Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences.

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity packs can fund consumption.
claims.quote: Prepaid capacity packs and pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription provide ways to fund that consumption.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription can fund consumption.
claims.quote: Prepaid capacity packs and pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription provide ways to fund that consumption.

claims.claim: Work IQ API reporting is separate and is not a Business Applications-only breakdown.
claims.quote: Direct calls through the Work IQ API are reported under Work IQ API. ... Its total is not a Business Applications-only cost breakdown.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps, so task consumption varies rather than having a fixed prompt price.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps. Work IQ includes deterministic operations and variable-cost contextual reasoning, so a prompt isn't necessarily a single fixed-price operation.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature pages publish no per-task Copilot Credit rate for Cowork business-context requests.
claims.quote: Searched: Cowork Business apps license pricing per task credits. Opened cowork-work-iq, understand-costs, plugins/cost-considerations and Work IQ api-overview; read Credit usage for Microsoft Copilot Cowork tasks search excerpts. No feature-specific per-task rate found.

claims.claim: Learn names no separate license for the Business apps plugin itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Cowork Business apps license pricing per task credits. Opened cowork-work-iq, understand-costs, plugins/cost-considerations, cowork-admin-governance and Work IQ api-overview. No separate Business apps plugin license found; parent-service access and consumption still apply.

claims.claim: Cowork experiences might vary with the organization's apps, licenses, policies and available services.
claims.quote: Some experiences might vary based on your organization's apps, licenses, policies, and available services.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[4].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Spending policies select users and services and provide policy and per-user consumption limits.
claims.quote: Spending policies let you choose the users and services covered, set a shared monthly limit, add a per-user limit, and receive alerts as consumption approaches a threshold.

claims.claim: Underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during consumption-based previews.
claims.quote: For consumption-based services, usage of underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during the preview period.

claims.claim: A Power Platform administrator must enable Work IQ for the environment.

claims.quote: For the model-driven app, the Enable M365 Copilot in model-driven apps setting (m365copilotmodelappenabled) must be set to Default or On.

claims.claim: Users need permission to the Power Platform environment, model-driven app and business data involved.
claims.quote: You need permission to access the Power Platform environment, model-driven app, and business data involved in your request.

claims.claim: Learn specifies AI Administrator for Microsoft 365 admin center connection settings.
claims.quote: AI Administrator role to work with settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Learn specifies Power Platform Administrator for environment participation and application-access settings.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator to configure environment settings.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is not currently available in sovereign or government clouds, including DoD, GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.claim: Plugin installation is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Plugins > Business apps (preview) > Install.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. In the Name column, select Business apps (preview). ... In the Business apps (preview) panel, select the Install button.

claims.claim: The qualified general package-block operation is POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.quote: Searched: Business apps copilotPackage Cowork Work IQ MCP block dependency; Business apps Package Management API Cowork. Opened cowork-work-iq and copilotpackage-block. The plugin page gives UI installation; the API reference does not identify this plugin.

claims.claim: The tenant audience setting is under Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Copilot > Settings. In Copilot settings, select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.

claims.claim: No API for the tenant business-applications audience setting is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications Work IQ tenant Graph settings API; Business Applications data in Work IQ API PowerShell Graph; Work IQ Business Applications Graph audience setting. Read default-settings, manage-ai-experience-access and quickstart. No matching audience-setting API found.

claims.claim: Environment Work IQ is reached through Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote: Select Manage, and select the environment. Select Settings > Product > Features. Locate Work IQ. Turn on Work IQ if it's currently off.

claims.claim: No API for the environment Work IQ setting is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment PowerShell Enable Power Platform API; Work IQ environment pac admin API enable settings; Work IQ Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironment. Read manage-participation and searched pac admin and PowerShell support references for Work IQ, WorkIQ and Dataverse intelligence: no matches.

claims.claim: The feature-specific App Access setup path is Security > Identity & access > App Access Control > environment > Enable.
claims.quote: Select Security > Identity & access. Select App Access Control. Select the environment in which you want to enable app access. Select Enable, and then select Save.
claims.fix: Add to the row note: 'The general App Access reference gives different labels: Security > Identity and access > App access control > environment > Set up app access control > Access control > Enabled; select an application and Block. See https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/control-app-access-environment#turn-on-enabled-mode.'

claims.claim: PATCH https://<organization>/api/data/v9.2/applications(<applicationid>) updates an Application record's access setting.
claims.quote: Update ... PATCH /applications(applicationid) ... Writable columns/attributes ... Access ... LogicalName ... access
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/application to sources: it explicitly documents the /api/data/v9.2/applications entity-set path used in the call. The cited table reference already supports PATCH and the access property.

claims.claim: The Application access property accepts 0 for Allowed and 1 for Blocked.
claims.quote: LogicalName | access ... Access Choices/Options ... 0 | Allowed ... 1 | Blocked

claims.claim: Updating an app's allowed or blocked status is separate from enabling environment-level App Access enforcement.
claims.quote: If you set some apps to Allowed or Blocked, you don't need to remove the setting when the app access control feature is turned off to Disabled. There are no app restrictions in this environment.

claims.claim: The general App Access documentation requires a managed environment.
claims.quote: Your environment must be a managed environment.

claims.claim: The usage-based billing Cost Management experience is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot and then the Cost Management node.

claims.claim: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies is automation for setting how much Cowork can consume.
claims.quote: List spendingPolicies | GET /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies | Get a list of spending policies. ... Update spendingPolicy | PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} | Update a spending policy.
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}' and docs with https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/spendingpolicy-update. Add to the note: 'The request body sets periodLimit and perUserLimit.' This reference explicitly lists both as updatable properties.

claims.claim: The listed Microsoft Graph package and cost-management APIs are beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Deactivation is reached through Power Apps > environment > More > Business skills > skill > Deactivate.
claims.quote: Go to Power Apps and select your environment. ... select More, and then select Business skills. ... Select a skill, and then select Deactivate from the command bar or the three-dot menu

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP delete_skill is the automation counterpart of the row's skill activation control.
claims.quote: Deactivating a skill preserves its content and version history. ... Deleting a skill is permanent and can't be undone.
claims.fix: Replace the API with kind 'rest', call 'PATCH /skills(<skillid>)', and docs https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/reference/entities/skill. Replace the deletion note with: 'The request body sets statecode to 1 (Inactive) and statuscode to 2 (Inactive) to deactivate the skill without deleting it.' The table reference documents SetState through PATCH and these exact state/status values.

claims.claim: The cited business-skills maker page lists no Dataverse MCP tool that deactivates a skill.
claims.quote: Searched: business skill deactivate API statecode delete_skill. Opened data-platform-business-skills and the Business Skill table reference. The maker page's MCP list is upsert_skill, delete_skill, search and describe; it lists no deactivate tool. A separate REST state-update operation exists.

claims.claim: Sharing is available through Share after selecting a skill on the Business skills page.
claims.quote: Select a skill, and then select Share from the command bar or the three-dot menu

claims.claim: The whole Work IQ MCP server can be blocked through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools. Select Work IQ MCP. Review its current availability. To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether blocking the whole Work IQ MCP server stops the Business apps plugin in Cowork.
claims.quote: Searched: Business apps copilotPackage Cowork Work IQ MCP block dependency. Opened cowork-work-iq, manage-ai-experience-access and business-applications-work-iq. They describe the plugin connection and whole-server availability separately, without stating this blocking dependency.

claims.claim: Enabling an experience does not itself grant business-data access.
claims.quote: Enabling an experience doesn't grant access to business data.

claims.claim: The consumption licensing model reflects the documented Cowork usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork uses usage-based billing. Access comes only from a spending policy that includes the user and selects Cowork.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to review skills shared with everyone has a corresponding sharing control row.
claims.quote: Review which skills are shared with everyone in an environment. ... Whether a business skill is active for agents to discover
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Review which skills are shared with everyone in an environment.' The existing skills row governs activation, not sharing; its brief Share note does not make it a sharing row. Do not add a control row as part of this correction.

claims.claim: Plugin installation can target All users or Specific users and groups.
claims.quote: In the Installed for field, select All users or Specific users and groups.

claims.claim: The quickstart gives the tenant audience setting a slightly different label from the default-settings reference.
claims.quote: Open the setting for Business Applications in Work IQ available to Copilot in Microsoft 365 Copilot.
